design_summary: Adopt one common observation, authorization, and recovery package after the corrections below. Keep observations.qnt independently importable, but review its integration with authorization and both profile harnesses together: several defects appear only across those interfaces. The existing effects and consumption modules provide useful arithmetic and exact-parent bookkeeping, not a complete authorization machine. The common layer should check finite, neutral operation views against signed policy clauses and current bindings. It must not interpret any candidate's execution language. Candidate-specific code supplies execution proposals and complete plan views; separate correspondence checks establish whether those views faithfully represent the candidate and frozen Core. Use an explicit operation lifecycle, a registry indexed by AuthorityKey, exact-parent residual transitions, independently signed recovery, and atomic commit updates. This recommendation concerns the common design only and selects none of A–D.

required_changes.location: Pure-function interface; Harness state and action boundary
required_changes.defect: The proposed generic interface hides information that the common checker must inspect. In particular, computeAfterResolvePreSignCheck receives an opaque plan parameter and one expected Core result, but no explicit complete transfer view or collection of planned steps. Parametric code cannot derive deposit effects, alternative outcomes, or slot-specific predecessor conditions from an arbitrary plan payload. Copying the payload into a check record is a binding operation, not a complete plan check. The operator declarations also use schematic explicit type-parameter lists, whereas the supplied Quint foundation uses type variables inferred from annotated parameters. Neither the signatures nor the generic harness should be treated as executable source as written.
required_changes.counterexample: Instantiate plan as an opaque finite identifier. Give two plans the same expected Core payment list: one performs only an authorized payout, while the other also accepts a wallet-to-escrow deposit. Deposits are absent from Core payments. A common checker receiving only the opaque plan and that payment projection cannot inspect the additional debit. Similarly, supplying one expected result for a two-slot plan gives it no inspectable second-slot effects or predecessor relation.
required_changes.proposed_change: Introduce a neutral resolved-plan view containing finite planned operation records: operation identity, original complete plan payload, artifact/call payload, transaction-time constraints, complete ordered effects, expected predecessor and successor bindings, applicable Core projection, and parent/slot dependencies. Represent alternatives explicitly. Make common pre-sign checks consume this view and the proposed unsigned policy. Candidate adapters remain responsible for producing and validating views against their own representations; they are not replaced with a shared interpreter or a solver-supplied approval boolean. Retain generic payloads for exact identity and equality only. Use the source-established Quint operator style, such as pure def f(x: T[p]), with bodies in implementation. Instantiate harness state variables at concrete payload types and instantiate each signing-profile constant explicitly.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Typecheck and execute a concrete types-and-initialization instance before adding lifecycle logic. Then show that two views differing only by an additional accepted deposit receive different authorization decisions, and that changing slot 2's effects or expected predecessor invalidates an after-resolve plan check. A concrete two-slot plan must pass without executing either slot during pre-sign checking.

required_changes.defect: The mandatory Core projection cannot honestly represent operations outside the E00 transaction slice. Cancellation changes authorization state without being a frozen Core transaction. Requiring every cancellation or evidence rejection to carry a CoreResultObservation encourages invented Core success or error values. Rejected(CoreError) also conflates actual Core rejection with envelope, signature, freshness, and recovery rejection.
required_changes.counterexample: Cancel an unused parent while leaving its escrow at ten. No compute_transaction call or Core constructor implements this revocation. Filling the mandatory coreProjection with accepted=true and unchanged state creates a claimed Core result for an operation that was never a Core transaction. Alternatively, inserting an error such as stale_signature conflicts with validFrozenCoreError.
required_changes.proposed_change: Use an explicit sum such as NoCoreProjection | HasCoreProjection(CoreResultObservation[c]). Distinguish Core transaction rejection from authorization and evidence rejection using separate reason carriers. Preserve a candidate's proposed Core result separately from whether the envelope permits its commitment: an agreement-legal payout rejected by authorization remains a rejected commit, even though its proposed Core calculation was accepted. Make CoreResultEvidence available only when an applicable result has the required independent correspondence evidence. Lifecycle-only operations carry the declared abstract evidence level.
required_changes.acceptance_test: An unused cancellation must have no Core projection, retain escrow ten, and produce no settlement claim. A genuine time_before_state Core failure must retain its exact Core error. An agreement-legal but unauthorized payout must expose the accepted proposed Core result while committing no ledger, continuation, or consumption changes.

required_changes.defect: The type sketch does not operationalize conditional policy alternatives. A conjunction of unconditional RequiresIncoming and RequiresOutcome conditions cannot directly express a disposition policy that permits settlement with incoming consideration and also permits a voluntary or deadline refund. The same issue occurs when a parent authorizes two installments but each transaction executes only one. The existing policyAllows function is a multiset predicate; it neither selects an authorized branch nor constrains order. This is a definite specification gap, not evidence of an already implemented bypass.
required_changes.counterexample: Give Alice's swap disposition an unconditional requirement to receive Bob's twenty TokenB. Settlement can pass, but a legitimate early refund with only Alice's funded escrow fails. Remove that requirement and a proposal paying Alice's ten TokenA to Bob without the reciprocal payment can satisfy Alice's debit bounds. For installments, placing both identical five-unit transfers in requiredEffects makes the first single-transfer fill fail; requiring only one globally does not by itself describe the remaining slot's authority.
required_changes.proposed_change: Represent signed alternatives as finite operation or outcome clauses. Each clause contains its activation condition, required and allowed effects, relevant incoming consideration, refund restrictions, capabilities, and parent/slot requirements. Evaluate conditions conjunctively within the selected clause, and require at least one complete applicable clause. Use exact ordered effect lists for these finite fixture clauses, retaining policyAllows as a multiplicity primitive where appropriate. Define BoundedIntent as a complete policy body without a resolved-plan binding, or define an explicit consistency predicate covering every duplicated and omitted field. Pre-sign checking and signing must bind the full policy, including validity, refund rules, debit locations, and implementation version.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Under one signed swap disposition policy, reach reciprocal settlement, voluntary refund, deadline refund, and early refund of only funded escrow. Reject Alice-to-Bob payment without the required reciprocal consideration. Reach the first and second installments separately, reject duplicate occurrences and wrong-slot use, and reject an effect-order mutation when the selected clause fixes order. Changing a refund destination or validity bound after pre-sign checking must invalidate signing.

required_changes.defect: Debit coverage cannot authorize an operation with no financial effects. Cancellation has an empty transfer list, so conjunction over affectedPrincipals can be vacuously true. The imported canCancelParent checks bookkeeping freshness and remaining allowance, but does not check a signature, caller authority, cancellation permission, or enforcement evidence. Prepared cancellation stores only an Entry, which is insufficient to bind its full authorization context.
required_changes.counterexample: Start with an unused parent and ten units in escrow. Let Mallory prepare the current initial Entry and request cancellation with effects=List(). The affected-principal set is empty, and canCancelParent(parent, entry, entry) is true. If commitFreshCancel uses only these advertised checks, Mallory revokes Alice's authority without an applicable signed cancellation permission.
required_changes.proposed_change: Make operation authorization explicit. Required policies are the union of debit-owner policies and policies required by the operation, including the exact parent's cancellation authority even when effects are empty. Carry a prepared cancellation record with the exact parent, entry, applicable signed policy, operation identity, predecessor, environment, and verification bindings. Its commit must check the signed cancellation rule and capability plus current evidence and the imported bookkeeping guard. Index applicable policies by AuthorityKey, with an explicit required-key set, rather than relying only on Principal -> AuthorityRecord.
required_changes.acceptance_test: With unchanged financial effects and entry, reject cancellation by Mallory, cancellation under a policy without CancelParent, and cancellation with unavailable signature evidence. An authorized cancellation must remain reachable. A cancellation verified before an environment change must fail at commit until freshly verified, even when its Entry still matches.

required_changes.location: Lifecycle records; Context; HarnessState; signing actions
required_changes.defect: The lifecycle lacks explicit storage and transitions for a draft policy, a resolved proposal before checking, multiple independently signed keys, and restarting verification after a first fill or rejection. A single phase and single optional pre-sign record do not specify how the parent and recovery policy coexist. The text excludes a signature/pre-sign cycle, but the interface leaves a second cycle or invalidation trap possible through whole-registry snapshots.
required_changes.counterexample: Pre-check Alice and Bob while both authority entries are vacant. Register Alice's signature. Bob's previously checked whole Context no longer equals the current Context. A design requiring all original checks to remain equal cannot complete the joint authorization; a design ignoring all registry differences could accept a relevant consumption change. Separately, after commitFirstFill enters Committed, the sketch provides no explicit transition explaining how a fresh cancellation and a newly signed recovery policy become active without losing the signed parent.
required_changes.proposed_change: Define finite per-key signing records and an explicit current operation/attempt record containing draft policy, optional resolved view, pre-sign result, and execution verification. Keep persistent authority and parent registries separate from attempt phase. For a conservative initial implementation, serialize per-key pre-check and sign actions and recheck a policy if its checked context changes. Pre-sign checks operate on unsigned policy content and declared premises; they must not require their own signature or realized settlement. Signing records the exact checked policy and registers it without changing finances. Execution verification occurs only after all required keys are signed. Add explicit begin-next-operation and rejection/retry transitions, plus prepare and commit paths for both installment slots.
required_changes.acceptance_test: For SignAfterResolve, demonstrate resolve -> unsigned complete-plan check -> sign -> execution verify -> authorized commit. For SignBeforeResolve, demonstrate bounded-policy check -> sign with no concrete plan recorded -> resolve -> execution verify -> commit. Reach both principals' swap signatures and both parent and recovery signatures without circular prerequisites. After a first fill and stale-cancel rejection, retain the parent record and reach fresh cancellation and recovery.

required_changes.location: AuthorityRecord; ParentRegistry; authority consumption functions; recovery functions
required_changes.defect: The bridge between one-shot nonce consumption and continuing exact-parent authority is not specified. AuthorityConsumed cannot mean both 'never applicable again' and 'usable for the second parent slot' without a separate rule. The imported consumption functions deliberately do not inspect the authority registry or apply financial effects. Recovery functions also need an explicit atomic relationship between refund, recovery-nonce consumption, and cancellation state.
required_changes.counterexample: Sign parent P, fill slot 1, and mark its nonce consumed. If principalAllows accepts only AuthorityRegistered, slot 2 becomes unreachable. If it accepts any consumed policy with the same key, substituting P' under nonce 0 can acquire residual authority. If refund updates the ledger before consuming recovery nonce 1, an intervening replay can attempt the same refund again. If unused cancellation leaves nonce 0 registerable, a new standalone policy can attempt to revive the cancelled authority.
required_changes.proposed_change: Specify an atomic transition table. First fill changes Registered(P) to Consumed(P, revision 1), claims exactly Parent(P), consumes slot 1, and commits its ledger/candidate successor together. Later fills require the exact retained signed policy, exact claimed parent, matching current entry, and validResidual; they update the consumed revision rather than acquiring a new nonce. Unused cancellation also consumes the parent key and claims that exact parent; post-fill cancellation advances its revision. Registry and parent revisions must agree. Recovery requires a separately registered signed nonce-1 policy, exact cancelled parent and current entry, the precise remaining refund, fresh verification, and sufficient escrow. One commit changes ledger, candidate successor, recovery consumption, and receipt together. Keep the cancelled parent and its remainingAllowance unchanged by recovery.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Reach two fills with one parent nonce while rejecting standalone nonce reuse, substituted parents, replayed slot 1, and enlarged residuals. Reach unused cancellation with parent revision 1 and post-first-fill cancellation with revision 2. Recovery must consume nonce 1 exactly once and leave parent cancellation and usedSlots unchanged. Every failed attempt must preserve ledger and both registries.

required_changes.location: VerificationRecord; evidence records; verificationValid; canCommit; environment transitions
required_changes.defect: The intended exact bindings are sound, but their required equalities and time interpretation remain incomplete. EvidenceValid is only a disposition; acceptance also requires its payload to equal the actual policy, state, or effects being checked. Transaction-time equality between two record fields does not establish its relation to physical time. The settlement premise also needs a clear distinction from a post-commit settlement receipt to avoid either a circular prerequisite or a fabricated claim.
required_changes.counterexample: Verify an otherwise allowed transfer at transaction time 2, advance physicalTime to 101, and obtain fresh evidence whose environment says 101 while continuing to propose transaction time 2. If validation checks only record-time equality, domain membership, and current environment equality, BeforeDeadline(100) still passes after physical expiry. Independently, attaching EvidenceValid for a different effect list must not validate the current proposal. Requiring a receipt of completed settlement before commit would make the intended positive path circular.
required_changes.proposed_change: Write explicit binding predicates: signatures bind the exact registered signed policy; state evidence binds the complete current predecessor; effect evidence binds the entire ordered actual effect trace; all required environments and mechanism/version fields agree; settlement evidence matches its applicable projection and declared level. For successful authorized fixture commits, set transactionTime equal to the sampled physical execution time. Continue permitting stale transaction times as adversarial proposals for Core rejection and envelope tests. Recheck these constraints at commit. Treat pre-commit settlement-related information as declared assumptions or expected results, and create a modeled execution receipt only after commit. Do not require a real settlement receipt as an input to its own creation.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Verify at time 2, advance to 100 or 101, and reject the old commitment without any financial or consumption change. Attempt a newly verified backdated successful fill and reject it. Preserve the exact Core time_before_state result when now=1 and Core minimum time is 2. Mutate each evidence payload while keeping its disposition valid and require rejection. A normal abstract-model commit must not require or manufacture a real settlement receipt.

required_changes.location: Complete observation shapes; E00 correspondence boundary
required_changes.defect: The Core carriers can be lossless for the bounded fixtures, but the required encoding contract is incomplete. A total account map replaces Python's sorted sparse tuple, principal and asset constructors replace structured Python identifiers, and a continuation table replaces a recursive contract. These transformations require explicit reversible mappings. Native enum or set iteration order cannot reproduce Python's canonical refund order. This is an unclosed correspondence obligation, not a claim that the proposed account map is inherently lossy.
required_changes.counterexample: After funding both canonical swap escrows, a Close reduction pays accounts in Python's canonical order. An extractor iterating a Quint set can emit Bob's refund before Alice's while preserving all balances and the same transfer multiset. A continuation represented by a current node index can also remain unchanged while the node table's payee is altered. An abstraction map that drops a present choice value zero changes ChoiceEquals(choice_id, 0) while preserving a map's default numeric value.
required_changes.proposed_change: Specify immutable bijections for fixture parties and tokens, an independently pinned canonical account/key ordering, zero-to-absent account decoding restricted to valid Core states, and exact OptionalInt choice decoding. Continuation encoding must preserve every constructor field, ordered When cases, action identities and bounds, observation values, amounts, timeout, and successors; decoding the complete table and root must reconstruct the exact Core contract. Reject unknown fixture identifiers instead of dropping them. Define validCoreObservation as a structural/emission validator, not an interpreter or correspondence oracle. The independent trace checker compares every decoded result field against frozen Python and independently checks complete transfers, including pre-input payments, the accepted deposit occurrence, and post-input payments in execution order.
required_changes.acceptance_test: For the canonical swap, fund Alice at 1 and Bob at 2, then accept choice 1 at 2: require the two ordered settlement payments, choice settle=1, empty accounts, Close, minimum time 2, and three reductions. With both escrows funded, no input at 100 must refund Alice then Bob with three reductions; supplied choice input at 100 must instead return contract_closed, zero reductions, empty payments/warnings/effects, and the exact predecessor. Test absent choice versus present zero, partial and non-positive payment warnings, out-of-fixture identifiers, and mutations of account ordering, continuation tables, extraction, and the independent abstraction map.

required_changes.location: Witness requirements and future S02-05/S02-09 coverage validation
required_changes.defect: The supplied machine-readable requirements list contains only the top-level cancellation witnesses. The observation design requires two specific recovery subscenarios, but those obligations are not encoded in this supplied requirements object. No validator implementation is supplied, so its behavior cannot be assessed. A machine checking only the listed witness names can accept cancellation flags with money still escrowed.
required_changes.counterexample: Provide paths that set cancelled=true for cancel-wins and fill-wins, then stop with escrow ten or five and no recovery signature or refund. Such paths satisfy those top-level names but violate both mandated recovery outcomes.
required_changes.proposed_change: Preserve every existing witness identifier and add structured required subscenario entries for cancel-wins/recovery-before-any-fill and fill-wins/recovery-after-first-fill. Require both signing profiles for the common harness and every candidate/profile combination at the later candidate gate. The coverage validator must replay or independently inspect complete paths and check exact financial and authority terminal states, including the stale-cancel rejection and fresh cancellation on the fill-wins path. Keep these requirements attached to S02-05 and S02-09.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Reject evidence with either subscenario missing, one signing profile missing, cancellation without refund, or refund without a separately signed and consumed recovery key. The unused path must end escrow=0, paidToBob=0, refundedToAlice=10, parent cancelled with no used slots, and recovery nonce consumed. The first-fill path must end escrow=0, paidToBob=5, refundedToAlice=5, usedSlots={1}, parent cancelled, and recovery nonce consumed; slot 2 must remain unauthorized.

required_changes.location: Finite fixture instantiation; registry initialization; harness termination
required_changes.defect: Finite principal, nonce, anchor, and version sets do not by themselves make the generic record state finite. Integer policy revisions, physical time, arbitrary strings, generic tables, effect-list lengths, and repeated diagnostic history remain unbounded unless the fixture restricts them. The proposed action list also does not explicitly include second-installment commitment or a semantic terminal predicate.
required_changes.counterexample: Permit repeated sign actions that increase policyRevision, or append every failed replay to a history list. The model has an unbounded state space despite using only Alice, Bob, Mallory and two nonce values. At the opposite extreme, treating the first Committed phase as terminal makes second-installment completion and recovery unreachable. Allowing an unrelated environment update can conceal lack of enabled lifecycle progress.
required_changes.proposed_change: Publish concrete finite domains and closure checks for all reachable payloads. Initialize authority registries over both domains, all principals, and nonce values 0 and 1; initialize all ledger and fixture choice keys. Bound or structurally eliminate repeated signature revisions and unbounded logs. Use the existing parent revision equation, whose reachable two-slot values are 0, 1, and 2, rather than a wrapping counter. Constrain environment movement to the declared finite monotone domains. Use fixed finite constructor/plan tables and bounded ordered effect lists. Define explicit terminal outcomes after complete settlement or completed recovery, and check that nonterminal attempts have a meaningful enabled transition or an explicitly classified rejection/abort outcome. Include commitSecondFill and prohibit a blanket stutter transition.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Check fixture-domain closure under every action and execute every concrete module with all constants supplied. Reach second-installment completion and both recovery terminals. Show that an exhausted environment domain does not strand a valid unfinished attempt. Record expected terminal stopping separately from unexpected deadlock, and report Apalache results as bounded-depth or complete-state exploration according to what was actually performed.

accepted_design_commitments: One combined common-foundation review unit is appropriate. Observation carriers remain a separate importable module; integration checks cover their use by authorization and recovery.
Frozen Python Core 0.0.0-e00.2 remains unchanged. The common package supplies no new Core constructor and makes no semantic-scope motion.
Plain Quint shared state matches the stated communication model. No distributed-message framework is needed for this experiment.
A, B, C, and D retain distinct execution representations. Common arithmetic, observation schemas, and authorization predicates do not choose their legal execution transitions.

Both signing profiles remain mandatory. After-resolve signing checks a complete resolved plan before signing; before-resolve signing checks bounded policy and enforcement identity without representing a concrete plan as pre-sign verified.

Every actual debit requires its principal's authority, and every applicable principal's incoming consideration and conditional terms must also hold. Operation authorization additionally covers effects-free cancellation.
Wallet and escrow locations remain distinct. Accepted deposits appear in complete transfers and do not become invented Core payments.

Ordered payment, warning, and transfer occurrences are preserved. Multiplicity checks use the existing arithmetic foundation without silently identifying repeated occurrences or replacing traces with net balances.
The exact error string, optional warning values, accounts, absent-versus-zero choices, complete continuation, minimum time, and reduction count are retained in applicable Core projections.

The supplied consumption bookkeeping correctly distinguishes paid quantity from remaining allowance and binds a claimed parent by complete equality. Its guards need authorization and atomic financial integration around them.
The initial installment escrow of ten is a declared fixture assumption. The signed parent authorizes two five-unit slots, and later residual use derives only from the exact consumed parent.
Cancellation revokes remaining payment authority without releasing escrow. Recovery is a distinct signed and verified operation under Alice nonce 1.
Both required recovery paths end with escrowBalance + paidToBob + refundedToAlice = 10. Remaining cancelled allowance is historical accounting, not spendable capability.
Resolve, pre-sign check, sign, environment change, execution verification, and commit remain separate where interleavings can invalidate bindings.
Invalid or unavailable required evidence fails closed. Valid dispositions remain declared model premises and do not establish cryptography, authenticated effect extraction, or settlement.

Correspondence extraction, its correctness oracle, and abstraction-map controls remain independently implemented. Mutations that are masked by another guard require a demonstrated redundancy explanation.
Mandatory named positive witnesses and negative controls precede any architecture comparison. No choice among A–D is justified by this proposal.
open_questions: The supplied evidence does not identify the concrete pinned Quint/Apalache versions or provide executable instances of the new types. Type inference, monomorphization, and backend tractability remain empirical checks. The proposed concrete-fixture route avoids relying on generic state variables or runtime reflection.

How large will exact policy, predecessor, and plan records make Apalache exploration? Start with exact records for correctness, then optimize only with an independently checked abstraction. State-count or timing measurements do not determine production cost.

Which finite adversarial fixtures will exercise all six frozen Core errors and both warning emitters? The canonical swap alone does not reach every error or warning; dedicated E00-compatible fixtures are needed.

For non-E00 candidate behavior, which operation-level observations are comparable across A–D, and which remain candidate-specific? This must be fixed in their later plans without inventing Core projections.

After the common design is corrected, the independent experts still need to reconcile any substantive disagreement about those corrections. Their delegated design signoff does not substitute for executable checks or select an architecture.
implementation_order: Revise the common type sketch and machine-readable obligations around the corrections above. Preserve the user's delegated expert design decision and remove obsolete text requiring a new human choice between combined and split packages.

Implement the neutral observation, policy-clause, operation, and evidence carriers with concrete finite fixture aliases. Add explicit absence for nonapplicable Core projections and initialize every required map key.
Typecheck and run initialization for both profile instances. Check fixture domains and structural Core emission validation before introducing lifecycle actions.

Implement unsigned pre-sign checks over complete neutral plan views and bounded policy bodies. Add separate signing records and exact-policy registration; demonstrate both profile orderings without signature or settlement cycles.

Implement full execution verification, operation-specific authorization, and current-context commit checks. Exercise policy substitution, zero-effect unauthorized cancellation, stale time/environment, and mismatched evidence payloads.

Integrate the existing consumption module through atomic registry/parent/ledger transitions. Demonstrate first fill, exact residual second fill, replay rejection, cancellation before any fill, and cancellation after a first fill.

Add separately checked and signed recovery policy lifecycles under nonce 1. Reach the two required recovery paths under both profiles, including prepared stale cancellation, its rejection, and fresh cancellation.

Implement the coverage validator obligations for the named subscenarios and complete terminal states. Keep deterministic scenarios in authorization_test.qnt and keep the operational step relation in the harness.

Run appropriate Quint typecheck, deterministic tests, and reproducible sampled witnesses, then the authorized Apalache checks with pinned tools and declared exploration depth. Record termination behavior and retain all counterexample paths.

Proceed to separate A–D candidate plans and implementations. Add independent frozen-Core codecs, trace checks, and abstraction-map mutations before any candidate correspondence claim or architecture selection.
scope_limits: This is an independent design proposal and design-signoff recommendation, not an implementation acceptance, Council gate verdict, proof, or S02 result.
The analysis uses only the supplied frozen source contents and necessary Quint guidance. No model or code tests were executed, and no proposed counterexample is presented as an observed execution.
Source digests below are the supplied evidence identifiers; they are not a claim of independently recomputed repository-file hashes.
The CLI credential failure is not evidence for or against this design. Model self-identification is not provider-identity evidence.
The recommendation does not reopen frozen Core, authorize Foreman development, or select A, B, C, or D.
The supplied effects and consumption modules are reviewed as source-level foundations here; their current test coverage and model-checking status are not established by the inline evidence.

Finite fixture checking cannot establish unbounded correctness, real signature authenticity, private-effect extraction, Compact/ledger correspondence, production cost, ACTUS coverage, cooperation, availability, or human preference.
Expected terminal stopping is allowed. An always-enabled no-op or unrelated environment transition must not be used as evidence that the authorization lifecycle can progress.
